title: Mini-Project: Build a GSD Command
objective: Apply everything from lessons 1-5 to add a new command to GSD

content.value:
You have traced the full command lifecycle -- from CLI entry point through the switch router, into tool modules, and back out through the output layer. Now prove you understand it by building something real.

Your task is to add a brand new command to GSD. This is not a quiz or a hypothetical exercise. You will create actual files in the GSD codebase, and a verifier will check your work structurally.

If you get stuck, use the hint command. Hints start vague and get more specific, but they never give you the code -- that part is yours.

When you are ready to check your work, run the verify command. When you want a nudge, run the hint command. You can run both as many times as you like.

Tip: if something goes wrong, remember that `git checkout` can undo your changes. You are working on the real codebase, but everything is recoverable.

content.task: Add a new 'echo' command to GSD that takes a message argument and outputs it using the standard GSD output pattern.
deliverables: A handler function in a lib/*.cjs file (e.g., get-shit-done/bin/lib/echo.cjs)
A new case in the gsd-tools.cjs switch statement that routes to your handler
Output that follows the GSD JSON/raw dual-output pattern

successCriteria:
Running --verify shows all checks passing: file exists, function exported, switch case added, output follows GSD pattern

Want to go deeper? Press [c] to copy this lesson to your clipboard and paste it into your favorite LLM for follow-up questions.
